I'm 38, working as a mechanical engineer at a large automotive company for 10 years, earning $95k with good benefits and pension. I've been offered a role at an electric vehicle startup at $130k but no pension and equity is mostly worthless. I have a daughter with special needs requiring therapy sessions, and my wife just went back to school for her nursing degree. We're comfortable but not wealthy. My current job has laid off people twice in my tenure but I survived. Should I take the startup risk?

I've been freelancing but only bringing in about $2k a month. The startup could turn into something big if they get their next funding round. I need to decide soon as my runway is shrinking. What would you do?

So my husband and I have been together for 6 years, married for 2. We met in grad school and he's always been the more laid-back one while I'm more ambitious. Recently I got offered a promotion at work that would take me from $75k to $110k but it requires relocating to our company's HQ in Chicago. We've been trying to start a family and he's worried about leaving his support system — his mom just got diagnosed with early-stage dementia and his sister lives nearby and helps out. He works remotely so he could keep his job. I'm worried if I turn down the promotion twice I'll get passed over for good. We've talked about it three times and keep going in circles. Any advice?

I'm 26, finishing my MSc in environmental science next month. I have $30k in student loans at 5.5% interest and I just got a job offer as an environmental consultant at $52k with a small firm, plus I'm considering applying for a PhD position that would pay $28k stipend but take 4 years. I have $15k saved from my part-time job. My dad thinks I should take the job and start paying down debt, but my thesis advisor says the PhD would open doors to research and policy roles I can't access otherwise. I'm torn because I do enjoy research but the money situation worries me. What should I prioritize?

I'm 55 and recently separated from my wife of 20 years. The house is going to be sold and I'll get about $180k from my share. I have a modest pension from my government job that will pay about $2,500/month if I retire at 62. I've been renting a one-bedroom apartment for $1,400/month but I hate the lack of space and thin walls. I'm thinking about buying a small condo for around $250k with the proceeds plus some of my savings. My financial advisor is pushing me toward index funds instead, saying real estate is illiquid and a hassle at my age. I travel a lot for work and would need to manage the property remotely sometimes. What makes more sense for my situation?

I'm 33, working as a nurse for 8 years in the UK NHS, currently on £38k. I've been accepted onto a physician associate program that would take 2 years full-time and I'd have to leave my job to study. The starting salary once qualified would be around £45-50k and there's more flexibility and variety. However, I'd lose my NHS pension contributions for 2 years, my husband would have to cover our mortgage alone on his £45k salary, and we'd need to dip into our emergency fund. We have a 4-year-old and another baby on the way. Is the career change worth the financial and personal strain right now?

I've been with my partner for 3 years and we're getting serious about marriage. They earn $80k as a graphic designer and I make $62k as a paralegal. We both have student loans — mine are $35k at 4.5% and theirs are $70k at 6.8%. We each contribute to our own debts and split rent 50/50 even though they earn more. We have about $20k combined in savings. When we talk about merging finances for marriage, they want to keep separate accounts and handle debts separately forever. I'm worried this will cause problems down the line. How do we navigate this?

I'm 45 and have been self-employed as a freelance graphic designer for 10 years. My income varies between $50k-80k a year depending on the economy. I've never contributed to a pension and only have $25k in savings. I'm recently divorced and my ex took half our assets. I know I need to save aggressively but I also need to update my equipment this year which will cost about $5k. I'm considering whether to get a part-time employed role to get pension contributions, but my clients would not be happy if I reduced my availability. How do I balance catching up on retirement savings with maintaining my income?

I'm 24, graduated with a biology degree last year and have been working as a lab technician for $42k. I hate the work — it's repetitive and there's no growth. I've been offered a place on a coding bootcamp that costs $15k and takes 6 months, which would qualify me for junior developer roles starting around $55k. I have $8k saved and my parents said they'd cover the rest of the bootcamp costs as a graduation gift. The thing is, I also got accepted to vet school which I applied to before I realized I didn't want to do biology anymore. Vet school is 4 years, costs $200k total, and starting salaries are around $80k. I feel like I'm running out of time to decide. What should I do?
